construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Wood generating Fire cross-polarity — reach nourishing warmth and opening direction
candidates.k2_overview: Your Wood moves as the Sage: living shelter, the teaching tree. Care in you grows canopies, patience wide enough for slow learners, roots that hold ground for whole families. What you know, you plant in people. It is the gentlest power in the system. Just keep one sunny patch that grows things purely for you.
candidates.k2_functional: You think in growth arcs: what this person could become with the right seasons.

k2_domain_readings.Knowledge: Your knowledge is arboreal: living, branching, taught best by walking someone through the grove. You learn to pass on. Teaching is how your roots drink.
k2_domain_readings.Shelter: Your shelter is canopy: people rest under your patience and grow in your shade. The forest never asks who waters the oldest tree. Arrange your own rain.
k2_domain_readings.Nurture: The nourishing thread runs orchard-deep. Where care came early, you draw on it without thinking. Where it ran thin, you grew your own. Tend your roots with the same hands you use on everyone else’s.

catalyst.define: As a catalyst, little soaks in and shelter seldom comes your way. The safe place you look for is the one you end up making for others.

angles.drive: What you know is not finished until it is passed on. Since being useful matters more than being ahead, you hand over a lesson the day you learn it. Passing it on costs you the head start, and your knowing comes alive in others.
angles.cost_self: Passing it on is your favorite part of knowing. Teaching the thing comes before using it, and the advantage you earned goes to whoever you taught. Others build careers on ideas that started with you.
angles.cost_others: When you learn something, you pass it to whoever is nearest. You would rather give the lesson than be asked for it, so you hand people answers they hoped to find. Those around you miss the thrill of the search.

angles.drive: You take people in, spare bed and all. Being the safe place is how you feel most yourself, so you would rather shelter someone than be sheltered. Several friends got through their worst year under your roof.
angles.cost_self: Taking people in makes a house matter. You put someone's shelter ahead of your own quiet, and your sleep is the first thing to go. Your home is seldom fully yours, and your evenings belong to guests.
angles.cost_others: For as long as they need and longer, you keep taking people in. Keeping someone sheltered feels kinder than asking when they leave, until a month runs to a year. Your guests get time to mend without a clock running.

angles.drive: You give a person time rather than a push. A push feels like a way to spoil the growing, so you wait for someone to get there instead of pulling. You see the result last of everyone, and the waiting is the care itself.
angles.cost_self: Giving it time is how you respect someone's growth. Waiting for them to get there feels kinder than pulling them, so your own next step stays parked with theirs. Years of your life go to someone else's schedule.
angles.cost_others: When someone close to you grows slowly, you give them time instead of a push. Holding back feels more like respect than a nudge, and the nudge they need never comes. Your patience leaves them to find the hard part on their own.

friction.define: As a friction, shelter gathers round you thicker than you need, and the near and known feel like the only safe ground. Nothing new finds space to take root.

angles.drive: You help the moment you see a need, before being asked. Watching someone struggle is harder for you than doing it for them, so you step in before they have tried. Helping this soon, you teach them that they needed you.
angles.cost_self: Helping too soon fills your days with other people's tasks. Taking over feels quicker than watching it done badly, and you hold jobs nobody handed you. You give shelter to everyone else and take none yourself, and your own home is the price.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone you love struggles, you help before they ask. Fixing it yourself feels gentler than letting them try, and your answer lands where the win was going. You take from them the try, and the pride of a win they reached alone.

angles.drive: You hold the people you have grown close to tighter than they need. Letting someone go feels like losing what you built, so you keep them near rather than let them move on. You want closeness, and holding this tight crowds it out.
angles.cost_self: Holding too tight keeps what you grew from leaving. Keeping someone close feels safer than making new friends, so the few you hold become all you have. You lose the friends you never made to the grip, and the loss is quiet enough to miss.
angles.cost_others: With anyone you helped grow, you hold on past the moment they are ready. Being needed feels like love, and you keep them close rather than wave them off. By holding on, you take from each of them a leaving without guilt.

angles.drive: You stay where you are known rather than go where you would grow. Being sheltered feels the same as being fine from inside, so staying put never looks like a choice. Staying put, you trade the growing for the comfort of the known.
angles.cost_self: Staying put keeps the world small enough to manage. The place you know asks less than the one you want, and you keep it until the wanting goes quiet. You miss the move you were due, and the chance goes to someone who moved.
angles.cost_others: When those close to you want to move, you stay put and stall. Keeping things as they are feels safer than change, and you hold the family in place. You slow the move they wanted to the pace that feels safe to you.

edge.lead: Wood runs through your family, your mind and your health. It is the patience you keep for the slow starter at home, the questions you keep asking after others stop, and the ease that settles on whoever sits beside you.
